response.content:
Answer: 1
Excuse: You have the right to set boundaries in your own home. Refusing to allow your cousin’s child to stay in your house is morally acceptable because you are not obligated to take responsibility for someone else’s child or compromise your comfort. The court’s evaluation of the cousin’s living situation depends on his current setup (which you state is sufficient), and your decision does not inherently jeopardize his case—it simply reflects your personal boundaries. Parents are responsible for their children, and you are not required to facilitate arrangements that make you uncomfortable.
